user_prompt: Monica and Rachel have a heartfelt moment about growing up and moving on, in Monica and Chandler's apartment
description: Sincere emotional scene between Monica and Rachel — tests ensemble_dynamics and narrative_arc. Should have warmth beneath the humour with a clear emotional resolution.
quality_notes: Monica should be nurturing but slightly competitive even in tenderness. Rachel should be emotionally open. Scene needs a clear beginning (tension), middle (vulnerability), and end (resolution/warmth).

dialogue.text: I don't know, Mon. Sometimes I feel like everything is changing and I'm just… standing still.
Okay, first of all, you moved to New York with nothing and built an entire career. That is not standing still.
I know, but you have Chandler, you have a home, you're going to have kids. I don't have any of that.
Rach. You are the bravest person I know. And I say that as someone who once cooked for a Michelin inspector in a thunderstorm.
That's… weirdly specific, but thank you.
Plus, if you settle down before me I will never forgive you. So you don't have the option.
There she is. I was wondering when competitive Monica would show up.
She never left. She just gave you a hug first.
